hints.title: Parity and Sorting Order
hints.text: The array length must be even. Sort changed array ascending so that the smallest available element must be an original number.

hints.title: Greedy Pairing Mechanism
hints.text: Use a frequency table. Whenever considering smallest remaining element x, find and consume one instance of two times x.

hints.title: Handling Zero Multiplicity
hints.text: When x is zero, it requires at least two available zeros in the frequency map to form a valid pair.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.time: O(N log N) sorting the doubled array of size N
complexity.space: O(N) to maintain value frequencies in counter
variables: N: number of elements in changed
complexity.notes: Greedy smallest-first pairing guarantees that no doubled value is mistakenly treated as an original.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Unordered matching can pair an original with an element that should have paired with an even smaller number.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Sorting orders candidate originals so greedy decrementing succeeds deterministically.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should check even length first, sort ascending, and carefully handle zero.
